item.title: Ash, Data and Costs Reshape Practical Choices
item.description: Flight disruption, data exposure and practical cost, travel and transport changes create several decisions to revisit.
item.content:encoded:
A volcanic disruption, data exposure and several concrete cost, travel and transport changes create new decisions this week.

  1. Indonesia ash shuts airports and disrupts Bali flights Anak Krakatau erupted on 6 September, sending ash as high as about 50,000 feet and temporarily suspending operations at six Indonesian airports including Jakarta; hundreds of flight movements were disrupted, with effects reported as far as Bali. Travellers routing through Indonesia should re-check same-day flight status. 6 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  2. Mathspace breach exposes 1.08 million Australia-NZ accounts Mathspace confirmed attackers downloaded data covering 1,079,819 students, parents or guardians, teachers and staff in Australia and New Zealand. Exposed fields can include names, email addresses, usernames, country, timezone and account-activity dates; passwords, SSO tokens and other customer authentication credentials were not exposed. Individual notifications began 6 September. 5-6 Sep 2026. Mathspace · Follow up
  3. Australian housing affordability hits a record low New data show a median-income Australian household earning about A$125,000 could afford only 12% of homes sold in the last financial year, while mortgage repayments reached 35.5% of average household income, the highest share since 1989. 5 Sep 2026. ABC · Follow up
  4. NZ banks pass the OCR rise into floating mortgages All five major New Zealand banks have announced higher floating mortgage rates after the 2 September OCR increase. Westpac’s variable home lending rises 0.25 percentage points from 7 September for new customers and 10 September for existing customers, while the other majors have also announced increases with their own effective dates. 2-3 Sep 2026. Westpac · 1News · Follow up
  5. Fiji’s new 5% tourism tax now applies to new bookings Fiji’s 5% Tourism Services Tax applies to qualifying tourism bookings made on or after 1 September. Bookings made before 1 September remain exempt even when the trip or service occurs later, so the practical price change now depends on when the booking was made. 1 Sep 2026. Fiji Times · Follow up
  6. Western Sydney’s new airport completes passenger-flight trial A Jetstar A320 completed a trial flight into Western Sydney International on 1 September, including an end-to-end passenger-process rehearsal. The airport’s first commercial passenger service is confirmed for 25 October, when Jetstar JQ362 departs for the Gold Coast. 1 Sep 2026. Jetstar · Follow up
  7. West Tarneit Station opens next Sunday Victoria has confirmed West Tarneit Station will open with the first train on 13 September. The new Geelong Line stop will have 689 trains a week, a four-bay bus interchange, 400 parking spaces, an accessible underpass and a new Route 186 bus connection. 2 Sep 2026. Victoria’s Big Build · Follow up
  8. Melton’s rebuilt station is now open The new elevated Melton Station opened to passengers on 1 September with four platforms, lifts, stairs and a 16-metre underpass. All four associated level crossings have been removed, and extended platforms are ready for nine-car VLocity trains planned for 2027. 1 Sep 2026. Victoria’s Big Build · Follow up
  9. Australia prepares algorithm opt-out rules for social media The federal government says it will release an exposure draft of its Digital Duty of Care this week. The proposed rules would require social-media services to offer users a way to turn off algorithmic feeds and would expose companies to penalties above A$100 million for specified breaches. 6 Sep 2026. ABC · Follow up
  10. Android’s September Drop adds new everyday tools Google’s September Android Drop is rolling out features including Google Keep integration in Messages and custom chat themes, while additional features include Gemini remembered-item locations in Find Hub, Guided Vision camera descriptions and Motion Assist on supported Android versions. Availability varies by Android version and rollout stage. 1-2 Sep 2026. Google · Follow up
  11. Windows 11 will auto-enable Memory Integrity more widely Microsoft will expand automatic activation of Windows 11 Memory Integrity on eligible PCs through October quality updates. Machines where the user explicitly disabled the feature are expected to remain disabled; affected users with older drivers or performance-sensitive games should know the security setting may change automatically. 2 Sep 2026. The Verge · Follow up
  12. EVA Air changes international baggage charges from 29 September EVA Air will change excess, overweight and oversized baggage charges and acceptance rules for travel on or after 29 September. Passengers who prepay eligible excess baggage at least four hours before departure receive a 10% discount. 3 Sep 2026. EVA Air · Follow up
  13. NZ Post cuts its domestic courier variable surcharge NZ Post’s domestic Courier total variable rate fell from 8.00% in August to 6.30% in September, reducing the variable surcharge component applied to affected courier pricing. 1 Sep 2026. NZ Post · Follow up
  14. Xero raises New Zealand subscription prices from October From 1 October, Xero’s New Zealand monthly prices rise from NZ$35 to $37 for Ignite, $83 to $89 for Grow, $110 to $117 for Comprehensive and $125 to $135 for Ultimate, excluding GST. Ultimate payroll overage above 10 employees also doubles from $1 to $2 per employee per month, and the multi-organisation discount begins to phase out. 1 Oct 2026. Xero · Follow up
  15. Selected NZ visitor and transit visas become online-only Immigration New Zealand says selected visitor and transit visa categories will stop accepting paper applications from 1 October and move to the enhanced Immigration Online system, changing the application route for affected people seeking to visit or transit New Zealand. 4 Sep 2026. Immigration NZ · Follow up
  16. NSW’s $100 private-car registration discount is now active Eligible private light-vehicle registrations in New South Wales now receive an automatic A$100 discount, while eligible motorcycles receive A$80 off. The discount applies to new and renewed registrations from 1 September 2026 through 31 August 2027. 1 Sep 2026. NSW Government · Follow up
  17. NSW energy-upgrade incentive rules change Monday Updated Energy Security Safeguard rules take effect on 7 September, changing parts of the Energy Savings Scheme and Peak Demand Reduction Scheme, including eligibility and co-payment settings for some air-conditioning upgrades and incentive settings for batteries and virtual power plants. 7 Sep 2026. NSW Government · Follow up
  18. Australia offers free fast-tracked qualifications to experienced tradies The Australian government announced a A$78 million programme offering free, accelerated recognition pathways for up to 6,000 experienced tradespeople, creating a new route for eligible workers to convert existing skills into Australian qualifications. 6 Sep 2026. Guardian · Follow up

item.title: Travel Access Expands as Australian Costs Shift
item.description: Travel access shifts while Australian finances, public transport and practical digital tools change.
item.content:encoded:
Travel access, Australian finances, public transport and several practical digital tools changed in concrete ways.

  1. SH6 gets another full daytime reopening Sunday State Highway 6 between Makarora and Hāwea is scheduled to open to ordinary traffic without escorted convoys from 8am to 5.30pm on Sunday 6 September, subject to weather; it then returns to three escorted weekday convoys from Monday. 4 Sep 2026. NZTA · Follow up
  2. Europe’s EES queue-relief switch-off ends 6 September The EU’s temporary mechanism allowing some border points to suspend biometric collection during extreme congestion ends after 6 September; from 7 September, non-EU short-stay travellers including New Zealanders remain subject to the fully operational Entry/Exit System’s facial, fingerprint and passport-data checks even when queues are heavy. 5 Sep 2026. EU · Times · Follow up
  3. Qantas and Condor link NZ to Europe on one ticket A new Qantas–Condor interline partnership is live, allowing connections between Australia, New Zealand and Condor’s European network through Bangkok, Johannesburg, Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Vancouver, Paris and Rome, with through-checked baggage; Qantas Frequent Flyer members can also redeem points for Condor seats. 1 Sep 2026. Condor · Follow up
  4. Australian home values fell across 95% of suburbs Cotality data for August show residential property values fell in 95% of Australian suburbs. 5 Sep 2026. Guardian · Follow up
  5. Australia releases 30% trust-tax draft Australia released exposure-draft legislation for the 30% minimum tax on discretionary trusts scheduled from 1 July 2028, including an option for trusts to elect fixed distributions to pre-nominated beneficiaries and exclusions for categories including charitable trusts, special disability trusts and superannuation funds. 3 Sep 2026. Australian Treasury — draft · Australian Treasury — settings · Follow up
  6. Gold Coast bus network expands from Monday From 7 September, the Gold Coast gets new Route 701 between The Pines and Robina via Elanora, Burleigh Heads and Varsity Lakes every 15 minutes, alongside 167 additional weekday trips and 112 additional weekend trips across the upgraded network. 17 Aug 2026. Queensland Government · Follow up
  7. Wairere Falls Track closes completely from Monday The Wairere Falls Track, carpark and toilets will close from 7 September for platform, bridge and other infrastructure work; DOC is targeting a full reopening by the end of November. 3 Sep 2026. DOC · Follow up
  8. Tongariro Northern Circuit full loop returns in December DOC says the Mangatepopo Track is on course to reopen in mid-December, restoring the complete Tongariro Northern Circuit loop, while the new Oturere Hut and campsite open for bookings from 18 December. 4 Sep 2026. DOC · Follow up
  9. Wellington–Upper Hutt trains become buses Sunday On Sunday 6 September, buses replace all daytime trains between Wellington and Upper Hutt on both the Hutt Valley and Wairarapa lines, changing same-day rail travel through the corridor. 6 Sep 2026. Metlink — Hutt Valley · Metlink — Wairarapa · Follow up
  10. Emirates holds Auckland cabin-crew recruitment Monday Emirates has scheduled an open cabin-crew recruitment day in Auckland for 9am on Monday 7 September at the Grand Millennium Hotel on Mayoral Drive, creating a concrete new application opportunity. 7 Sep 2026. Emirates Careers · Follow up
  11. Wellington gets a new waterfront art trail Bee in the City launches on 14 September and runs to 8 November along the Wellington waterfront, adding a free trail of 30 giant bee sculptures with a supporting map and app. 14 Sep 2026. WellingtonNZ · Follow up
  12. Te Papa opens five-year Māori carving exhibition Te Papa’s new He Toi Whakairo exhibition is now open, presenting seven centuries of Māori carving in a long-running exhibition scheduled for five years and adding a substantial new museum option in central Wellington. 29 Aug 2026. Te Papa · Follow up
  13. Qantas doubles Brisbane–Palau flights for peak season Qantas will add a second weekly Brisbane–Koror service from December 2026 through March 2027 and has extended the Palau Paradise Express programme through 30 November 2027, adding another practical Pacific travel option via Australia. 2 Sep 2026. Australian Government · Follow up
  14. Google Pics is now generally available Google Pics is generally available for eligible Workspace and Google AI plans, adding prompt-based image generation, object-level local editing, reformatting and translation of individual text elements, with rollout beginning 1 September. 1 Sep 2026. Google Workspace · Follow up
  15. Gemini gets global music generation with Lyria 3.5 Google made Lyria 3.5 available globally in Gemini, letting users create vocal or instrumental tracks from prompts and templates; the model is also available through the API, AI Studio, Google Vids and Flow Music. 4 Sep 2026. Google · Follow up
  16. Google Vids can turn documents into video summaries Google Vids can now generate video summaries from Google Docs, PDFs and Word files, creating a script, narration and visuals automatically for eligible Workspace and AI plans; rollout is already underway. 2 Sep 2026. Google Workspace · Follow up
  17. Uber starts supervised autonomous rides in London London riders requesting UberX, Uber Electric or Uber Comfort can now be matched at no extra cost with an all-electric Wayve autonomous vehicle carrying a human safety driver, marking the start of supervised autonomous ride-hailing on the Uber network in the UK. 3 Sep 2026. Uber · Follow up
  18. Zoox robotaxis now serve Las Vegas airport Zoox has added Harry Reid International Airport to its Las Vegas robotaxi service, with driverless pickups and drop-offs at both terminals near baggage claim, creating a new ground-transport option for Las Vegas arrivals. 3 Sep 2026. Las Vegas Sun · TechCrunch · Follow up
